raw.quick_summary: An undo history is modeled as a bounded sequence in which new actions are appended on the right and undo removes the rightmost, most recent action. A deque can support both ends, although this example uses only the right end.

key_concepts.explanation: A bounded sequence of actions that records operations so they can be undone in reverse order.
A new action is added to the right end of the history.
Undo removes and returns the action at the right end, which is the most recent action.
The history has a maximum capacity; in the example, it has room for six actions.
A double-ended queue that supports appending and popping at either end; this example uses only its right end.
Undo is unavailable when the history contains no actions.

learning_path.title: Modeling Undo with a Right-End Deque
learning_path.reason: The lesson follows the source's operation sequence from representation, through adding and undoing actions, to boundary behavior and the deque abstraction.

steps.title: Represent the undo history
steps.learning_goal: Understand the history as a bounded ordered sequence.
steps.explanation: An undo history stores actions in the order they were performed and has a maximum capacity, such as room for six actions.
steps.connection_to_previous: This establishes the data structure before applying operations to it.

steps.title: Append new actions
steps.learning_goal: Understand how a new action changes the history.
steps.explanation: New actions are added on the right. Starting with Draw and Color, appending Move produces Draw,Color,Move.
steps.connection_to_previous: Once the history is defined, appending shows how new actions enter it.

steps.title: Undo the most recent action
steps.learning_goal: Understand why undo removes the rightmost action.
steps.explanation: Undo pops the rightmost action and returns it. For Draw,Color,Move, undo returns Move and leaves Draw,Color.
steps.connection_to_previous: Undo operates on the state produced by appending actions.

steps.title: Handle empty history and deque behavior
steps.learning_goal: Recognize the empty-case rule and the broader deque abstraction.
steps.explanation: Undo is unavailable when the history is empty. Although a deque supports both ends, this teaching example uses only its right end for appending and popping.
steps.connection_to_previous: After understanding normal undo, the empty case defines the operation's boundary and the deque clarifies the underlying structure.

checkpoint_questions.question: Starting with Draw,Color, what history results from appending Move on the right?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Appending on the right places Move after Draw and Color.

checkpoint_questions.question: If the history is Draw,Color,Move, what does one undo do?
checkpoint_questions.explanation: Undo pops the rightmost, most recent action: Move.

checkpoint_questions.question: What should happen when undo is requested on an empty history?

options.text: It removes the first action ever added

checkpoint_questions.explanation: There is no action to pop when the history is empty, so undo is unavailable.

primary_visualization.reason: The core idea is an ordered process: actions are appended, the latest action is popped during undo, and the empty state prevents further undo.
